Details of its internal structure are unknown from this header.

functions.name: projectm_create
functions.description: Creates and initializes a new projectM instance and returns an opaque handle. Intended to be called after a suitable OpenGL context has been created and made current; otherwise creation may fail and return NULL. Use the returned handle with other projectM API calls and destroy it with projectm_destroy() when done.
requirements: Must be called when a valid and sufficient OpenGL context is initialized and current; otherwise it may return NULL.
Caller must check the return value for NULL before using the handle.
The returned handle must be passed to other projectM API calls that require an instance.
Each successfully created instance must eventually be destroyed with projectm_destroy().

functions.name: projectm_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a projectM instance and frees associated resources. After this call, the handle becomes invalid and must not be used in any further API calls.
requirements: instance must be a valid handle previously returned by projectm_create() (or projectm_create_settings()).
instance must not be used after this function returns.
Do not call more than once on the same instance handle.

functions.name: projectm_load_preset_file
functions.signature: void projectm_load_preset_file(projectm_handle instance, const char* filename, bool smooth_transition);
functions.description: Loads and switches to a preset from a file path or supported URL. Supports local filesystem paths, file:// URLs, and the special idle:// URL for the default idle preset. If loading fails, the current preset continues; any ongoing transition is finished immediately regardless of success. If smooth_transition is true, the preset switch is blended smoothly.
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM handle.
filename must be a non-NULL C string representing either a standard local path, a file:// URL, or the special idle:// URL.
Other URL schemes are not supported and will cause a loading error.
If called during an active transition, the transition will complete immediately (even if loading fails).

functions.name: projectm_load_preset_data
functions.signature: void projectm_load_preset_data(projectm_handle instance, const char* data, bool smooth_transition);
functions.description: Loads and switches to a preset provided as in-memory data. The data is currently assumed to be in Milkdrop format. If loading fails, the current preset continues; any ongoing transition is finished immediately. If smooth_transition is true, the preset switch is blended smoothly.
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM handle.
data must be a non-NULL C string containing preset contents in Milkdrop format.
If called during an active transition, the transition will complete immediately (even if loading fails).

functions.name: projectm_reset_textures
functions.description: Clears and reloads all textures used by projectM, including the main rendering texture. Intended for use after texture paths change; may introduce a brief rendering lag.
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM handle.
May temporarily impact rendering performance; callers should avoid calling in time-critical sections if a brief lag is unacceptable.

functions.name: projectm_get_version_components
functions.signature: void projectm_get_version_components(int* major, int* minor, int* patch);
functions.description: Writes the runtime library version components (major, minor, patch) into the provided pointers. Any component that is not needed may be passed as NULL.
requirements: If non-NULL, each of major, minor, and patch must point to writable int storage.
Any unwanted component pointers may be NULL.

functions.name: projectm_get_version_string
functions.description: Returns a newly allocated C string containing the runtime library version in the form major.minor.patch. The caller must free the returned string with projectm_free_string() when no longer needed.
requirements: Caller must free the returned string using projectm_free_string(); do not free with standard free().
Returned pointer may be NULL in error conditions (not specified); caller should handle a NULL return defensively.

functions.name: projectm_get_vcs_version_string
functions.description: Returns a newly allocated C string describing the VCS revision the library was built from (often a Git commit hash). Useful for diagnostics and bug reports. The caller must free the returned string with projectm_free_string() when no longer needed.
requirements: Caller must free the returned string using projectm_free_string(); do not free with standard free().
Returned pointer may be arbitrary text; caller should not assume a specific format and should handle a NULL return defensively (not specified).

functions.name: projectm_opengl_render_frame
functions.description: Render a single projectM visualization frame to the current OpenGL render target. Typical usage is per-frame in a render loop after a valid OpenGL context is made current and the projectM instance is initialized.
requirements: instance must be a valid, initialized projectM instance handle
An active, current OpenGL context must exist on the calling thread before invoking this function
This function performs no explicit error reporting; callers should assume no return status is provided

functions.name: projectm_opengl_render_frame_fbo
functions.description: Render a single projectM visualization frame into a user-supplied OpenGL framebuffer object (FBO) identified by framebuffer_object_id. Use when directing output away from the default framebuffer (e.g., offscreen rendering or post-processing pipelines).
requirements: instance must be a valid, initialized projectM instance handle
An active, current OpenGL context must exist on the calling thread before invoking this function
framebuffer_object_id must reference a valid, existing OpenGL framebuffer object owned/managed by the caller
The target FBO should be complete and in a state suitable for drawing (e.g., attachments sized as desired); otherwise rendering results are undefined
This function performs no explicit error reporting; callers should assume no return status is provided

functions.name: projectm_opengl_burn_texture
functions.signature: PROJECTM_EXPORT void projectm_opengl_burn_texture(projectm_handle instance, uint32_t texture, int left, int top, int width, int height);
functions.description: Burn (blit) the provided OpenGL texture into the active preset’s main texture. During preset transitions, the image is applied to both active presets. Position and size are specified in screen coordinates; negative width flips horizontally and negative height flips vertically.
requirements: instance must be a valid, initialized projectM instance handle
An active, current OpenGL context must exist on the calling thread before invoking this function
texture must be a valid OpenGL texture name (ID) referring to an existing texture object
left and top are screen-space offsets; width and height are screen-space extents; negative width flips horizontally and negative height flips vertically (as documented)
This function performs no explicit error reporting; callers should assume no return status is provided

functions.name: projectm_pcm_get_max_samples
functions.description: Returns the maximum number of audio samples that the internal audio buffer will store per channel. If more samples than this are provided in a single update, only up to this many per channel are kept and the remainder are discarded. Use this to size or chunk audio submissions to projectM.

functions.name: projectm_pcm_add_float
functions.signature: void projectm_pcm_add_float(projectm_handle instance, const float* samples, unsigned int count, projectm_channels channels);
functions.description: Adds new 32‑bit floating‑point PCM samples to the projectM instance’s internal audio buffer. Input is expected as interleaved channels if channels > 1 (for stereo, LRLRLR). Data is internally converted to 2‑channel float; mono inputs are duplicated to two channels. If more than the internal per‑channel maximum is submitted, excess samples are discarded.
requirements: instance must be a valid, initialized projectM instance handle (inferred from parameter type).
samples must point to at least count * channels contiguous float elements; for stereo, data must be interleaved LRLRLR (explicit).
Each sample value is expected to be within [-1.0, 1.0] (explicit).
count is the number of samples per channel; total samples provided must match count * channels (explicit/inferred).
channels must be PROJECTM_MONO, PROJECTM_STEREO, or a numeric channel count (explicit).
If the number of samples per channel exceeds projectm_pcm_get_max_samples(), only up to that many per channel are stored; the remainder are discarded (explicit).

functions.name: projectm_pcm_add_int16
functions.signature: void projectm_pcm_add_int16(projectm_handle instance, const int16_t* samples, unsigned int count, projectm_channels channels);
functions.description: Adds new 16‑bit signed PCM samples to the projectM instance’s internal audio buffer. Input is interleaved if channels > 1 (for stereo, LRLRLR). Data is internally converted to 2‑channel float; mono inputs are duplicated to two channels. Submissions exceeding the internal per‑channel maximum are truncated.
requirements: instance must be a valid, initialized projectM instance handle (inferred from parameter type).
samples must point to at least count * channels contiguous int16_t elements; for stereo, data must be interleaved LRLRLR (explicit/inferred).
count is the number of samples per channel; total samples provided must match count * channels (explicit/inferred).
channels must be PROJECTM_MONO, PROJECTM_STEREO, or a numeric channel count (explicit).
If the number of samples per channel exceeds projectm_pcm_get_max_samples(), only up to that many per channel are stored; the remainder are discarded (explicit).

functions.name: projectm_pcm_add_uint8
functions.signature: void projectm_pcm_add_uint8(projectm_handle instance, const uint8_t* samples, unsigned int count, projectm_channels channels);
functions.description: Adds new 8‑bit unsigned PCM samples to the projectM instance’s internal audio buffer. Input is interleaved if channels > 1 (for stereo, LRLRLR). Data is internally converted to 2‑channel float; mono inputs are duplicated to two channels. Submissions exceeding the internal per‑channel maximum are truncated.
requirements: instance must be a valid, initialized projectM instance handle (inferred from parameter type).
samples must point to at least count * channels contiguous uint8_t elements; for stereo, data must be interleaved LRLRLR (explicit/inferred).
count is the number of samples per channel; total samples provided must match count * channels (explicit/inferred).
channels must be PROJECTM_MONO, PROJECTM_STEREO, or a numeric channel count (explicit).
If the number of samples per channel exceeds projectm_pcm_get_max_samples(), only up to that many per channel are stored; the remainder are discarded (explicit).

functions.name: projectm_set_preset_switch_requested_event_callback
functions.signature: PROJECTM_EXPORT void projectm_set_preset_switch_requested_event_callback(projectm_handle instance, projectm_preset_switch_requested_event callback, void* user_data);
functions.description: Registers or removes the callback that projectM invokes whenever a preset switch is requested. Pass a non-null function pointer to start receiving events; pass NULL to remove the previously registered callback. The provided user_data pointer is stored and returned to the callback on each invocation. Only one callback can be registered per projectM instance.
requirements: instance must be a valid, initialized projectM instance handle.
callback may be NULL to remove any previously registered callback; otherwise it must be a valid function of type projectm_preset_switch_requested_event.
Only one callback can be registered per projectM instance at a time.
user_data, if non-null, should remain valid for the lifetime of the registration (until the callback is removed or the instance is destroyed).

functions.name: projectm_set_preset_switch_failed_event_callback
functions.signature: PROJECTM_EXPORT void projectm_set_preset_switch_failed_event_callback(projectm_handle instance, projectm_preset_switch_failed_event callback, void* user_data);
functions.description: Registers or removes the callback that projectM invokes when a preset change fails. Pass a non-null function pointer to receive failure notifications; pass NULL to remove the callback. The provided user_data pointer is stored and returned to the callback on each invocation. Only one callback can be registered per projectM instance. Note: within the callback, the preset filename and error message pointers provided by projectM are only valid during the callback invocation and must be copied if needed later.
requirements: instance must be a valid, initialized projectM instance handle.
callback may be NULL to remove any previously registered callback; otherwise it must be a valid function of type projectm_preset_switch_failed_event.
Only one callback can be registered per projectM instance at a time.
user_data, if non-null, should remain valid for the lifetime of the registration (until the callback is removed or the instance is destroyed).
Within the registered callback, any preset_filename and message strings received are only valid for the duration of the callback and must be copied if they need to be retained afterward.

functions.name: projectm_write_debug_image_on_next_frame
functions.signature: PROJECTM_EXPORT void projectm_write_debug_image_on_next_frame(projectm_handle instance, const char* output_file);
functions.description: Schedules a one-time dump of the main texture to a BMP image file. The dump occurs on the next render cycle after the main texture is rendered and before any composite shaders are applied. If output_file is NULL, the image is written to the current working directory with a timestamped name. Use this to inspect the main texture contents passed between frames; it does not capture the final post-composite framebuffer. To capture the final output, dump the main framebuffer after calling projectm_render_frame() on the application side.
requirements: instance must be a valid, initialized projectM instance handle.
Call this before the next render of the instance; the dump is performed for the next frame only.
If output_file is not NULL, it must point to a valid, writable filesystem location for the process.
The produced image reflects the main texture prior to composite shader application; it will not include composite effects.

functions.name: projectm_set_log_callback
functions.signature: PROJECTM_EXPORT void projectm_set_log_callback(projectm_log_callback callback, bool current_thread_only, void* user_data);
functions.description: Registers or removes a logging callback that projectM will invoke for each emitted log message. The callback can be installed globally or only for the calling thread based on current_thread_only. If both a global and a thread-specific callback are set, the thread-specific one is used. The callback executes in the same thread as the projectM API call that produced the log. Pass NULL as callback to remove the callback (globally or for the current thread, respectively). Messages may contain line breaks. The callback receives the message, its log level, and the user_data pointer provided here.
requirements: callback may be NULL to remove a previously set callback (global or thread-specific based on current_thread_only).
If current_thread_only is true, the callback is set only for the calling thread; otherwise it is set globally.
Inside the callback, the message pointer is only valid during the callback invocation; copy the string if it must be used after the callback returns.
Do not free the message pointer provided to the callback.
If multiple projectM instances log concurrently in different threads, the application's logging code (inside the callback) must be thread-safe.
user_data is an opaque pointer supplied here and will be passed back to the callback unchanged.

functions.name: projectm_set_log_level
functions.signature: PROJECTM_EXPORT void projectm_set_log_level(projectm_log_level log_level, bool current_thread_only);
functions.description: Sets the minimum log level at which the registered logging callback will be invoked. If log_level is PROJECTM_LOG_LEVEL_NOTSET, the global or default setting will be used. The level can be applied globally or only to the calling thread depending on current_thread_only. Note: The docstring mentions an instance parameter, but the function signature only accepts log_level and current_thread_only; the setting is instance-independent per the logging API description.
requirements: log_level must be a valid projectm_log_level value; PROJECTM_LOG_LEVEL_NOTSET selects the global/default level.
If current_thread_only is true, the log level change applies only to the calling thread; otherwise it applies globally.

functions.name: projectm_alloc_string
functions.description: Allocate a zero-initialized character buffer intended for use as a string and return its pointer. Memory allocated by this function must be released with projectm_free_string; do not use free or delete. Whether the requested length should include space for a terminating null byte is not documented; callers should account for this uncertainty when choosing length.
requirements: Caller must pass a length value of type unsigned int; exact valid range is not documented.
Caller must release the returned pointer with projectm_free_string; using free/delete is not allowed.
Returned memory is zero-initialized upon allocation.
The API does not document whether length should include space for a null terminator; this is unknown.
The API does not document whether the function can return NULL on allocation failure; this is unknown.

functions.name: projectm_free_string
functions.description: Free memory previously allocated for a string by projectm_alloc_string, or free (const) char* pointers returned by other projectM API calls. Must not be used to free memory allocated by standard allocators like malloc/new; likewise, free should not be used on pointers intended for this function. Behavior for a NULL pointer is not documented.
requirements: str must be a pointer returned by projectm_alloc_string or a (const) char* returned by a projectM API call.
Do not pass pointers allocated via malloc, new, or pointing to static/global or string literal storage.
After calling this function, the pointer must not be dereferenced or used again (no use-after-free).
Whether passing NULL is permitted is not documented and thus unknown.

functions.name: projectm_set_texture_search_paths
functions.signature: void projectm_set_texture_search_paths(projectm_handle instance, const char** texture_search_paths, size_t count)
functions.description: Sets the list of filesystem search paths used to locate textures. Calling this clears and reloads all textures (including the main rendering texture) and may introduce a short rendering stall. Use when the set of texture directories changes.
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM instance handle.
texture_search_paths must reference an array of count pointers to null-terminated strings.
count specifies the number of entries in texture_search_paths.
Calling may clear and reload textures and briefly delay rendering.

functions.name: projectm_set_frame_time
functions.description: Overrides the timebase used for animations with a user-specified fractional-seconds timestamp. Values >= 0 switch to the user timebase; values < 0 revert to system clock time. Useful for offline/non-realtime rendering.
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM instance handle.
If using user-specified time, pass a value >= 0; pass a value < 0 to use the system clock.
Frequent switching between user and system time can cause visual artifacts; prefer consistency.
If using this feature, setting the first frame to 0.0 is recommended.

functions.name: projectm_get_last_frame_time
functions.description: Returns the fractional-seconds time value actually used to render the last frame. If a user frame time was set, that value is returned; otherwise the system-clock-based time since projectM start.
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM instance handle.

functions.name: projectm_set_beat_sensitivity
functions.description: Sets the beat detection sensitivity factor used by projectM.
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM instance handle.

functions.name: projectm_get_beat_sensitivity
functions.description: Returns the current beat detection sensitivity factor.
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM instance handle.

functions.name: projectm_set_hard_cut_duration
functions.description: Sets the minimum time a preset must be displayed before a beat-triggered hard cut (instant transition) is allowed.
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM instance handle.
To effectively disable hard cuts, set this to a value higher than the preset duration (informational guidance).

functions.name: projectm_get_hard_cut_duration
functions.description: Returns the minimum display time before a hard cut can occur.
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM instance handle.

functions.name: projectm_set_hard_cut_enabled
functions.description: Enables or disables beat-triggered hard cuts. Even when enabled, hard cuts only occur if the hard cut duration is less than the preset duration.
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM instance handle.
For hard cuts to take effect, the hard cut duration must be set lower than the preset duration (library behavior note).

functions.name: projectm_get_hard_cut_enabled
functions.description: Returns whether hard cuts are currently enabled.
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM instance handle.

functions.name: projectm_set_hard_cut_sensitivity
functions.description: Sets the volume-difference threshold used by beat detection to trigger a hard cut.
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM instance handle.

functions.name: projectm_get_hard_cut_sensitivity
functions.description: Returns the current hard cut sensitivity (volume-difference threshold).
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM instance handle.

functions.name: projectm_set_soft_cut_duration
functions.description: Sets the duration of a soft transition (smooth blend) between presets.
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM instance handle.

functions.name: projectm_get_soft_cut_duration
functions.description: Returns the current soft transition duration between presets.
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM instance handle.

functions.name: projectm_set_preset_duration
functions.description: Sets the typical maximum display duration of a preset before initiating a soft cut. Hard cuts, if any, happen before this duration.
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM instance handle.

functions.name: projectm_get_preset_duration
functions.description: Returns the configured preset display duration before a soft cut is initiated.
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM instance handle.

functions.name: projectm_set_mesh_size
functions.signature: void projectm_set_mesh_size(projectm_handle instance, size_t width, size_t height)
functions.description: Sets the per-pixel equation mesh resolution. Values are internally clamped to [8, 300] for each axis, and odd values are incremented to the next even number.
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM instance handle.
Width and height are size_t values; the library clamps them to [8, 300] and adjusts odd values to even.

functions.name: projectm_get_mesh_size
functions.signature: void projectm_get_mesh_size(projectm_handle instance, size_t* width, size_t* height)
functions.description: Retrieves the current per-pixel equation mesh resolution.
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM instance handle.
width must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the mesh width.
height must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the mesh height.

functions.name: projectm_set_texel_offset
functions.signature: void projectm_set_texel_offset(projectm_handle instance, float offset_X, float offset_y)
functions.description: Applies sub-texel offsets used for main texture lookups in the warp shader to mitigate potential vendor-specific sampling drift. Milkdrop used 0.5 for both axes; OpenGL typically does not require it.
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM instance handle.

functions.name: projectm_get_texel_offset
functions.signature: void projectm_get_texel_offset(projectm_handle instance, float* offset_X, float* offset_y)
functions.description: Retrieves the currently configured sub-texel offsets for main texture lookups in the warp shader.
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM instance handle.
offset_X must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the horizontal offset.
offset_y must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the vertical offset.

functions.name: projectm_set_fps
functions.description: Sets the current or average frames-per-second value of the host application. Passed through to presets for their internal calculations; not otherwise used by the library.
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM instance handle.
Caller should periodically update this value with the application’s measured/average FPS (usage guidance).

functions.name: projectm_get_fps
functions.description: Returns the current/average FPS value set by the application. If not explicitly set, a default value of 60 is used.
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM instance handle.

functions.name: projectm_set_aspect_correction
functions.description: Enables or disables aspect ratio correction for presets that support it to avoid shape distortion on non-square viewports.
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM instance handle.

functions.name: projectm_get_aspect_correction
functions.description: Returns whether aspect ratio correction is enabled.
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM instance handle.

functions.name: projectm_set_easter_egg
functions.description: Sets the 'easter egg' sigma multiplier used by the Gaussian sampler that randomizes preset display duration. Values <= 0 are ignored and a default of 1.0 is used.
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM instance handle.
To change the value, pass a number greater than 0; otherwise 1.0 will be used.

functions.name: projectm_get_easter_egg
functions.description: Returns the current 'easter egg' value (sigma multiplier for randomized preset duration).
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM instance handle.

functions.name: projectm_set_preset_locked
functions.description: Locks or unlocks the current preset. When locked, automatic preset transitions (hard and soft cuts) are disabled; programmatic preset switches still occur.
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM instance handle.

functions.name: projectm_get_preset_locked
functions.description: Returns whether the current preset is locked (automatic transitions disabled).
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM instance handle.

functions.name: projectm_set_window_size
functions.signature: void projectm_set_window_size(projectm_handle instance, size_t width, size_t height)
functions.description: Sets the current viewport size in pixels. Must be called with non-zero dimensions to render anything. Internal textures are reallocated on the next frame only if a dimension changed. Calling every frame with unchanged size is harmless.
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM instance handle.
To render output, both width and height must be non-zero (library behavior note).

functions.name: projectm_get_window_size
functions.signature: void projectm_get_window_size(projectm_handle instance, size_t* width, size_t* height)
functions.description: Returns the current viewport size in pixels.
requirements: instance must be a valid projectM instance handle.
width must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the current width.
height must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the current height.

functions.name: projectm_touch

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Data type: filesystem path
# Used by stubs:
# - projectm_write_debug_image_on_next_frame: FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() (a single writable output path)
# - projectm_set_texture_search_paths: FUZZ_PARAM_STR() repeated to form an array of C strings (directory/search paths)
#
# Generator strategy:
# We construct a single bytes buffer that contains multiple NUL-terminated strings (C strings).
# The fuzzing runtime will slice this buffer for successive FUZZ_PARAM_STR / FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME calls.
#
# We include a diverse set of valid filesystem paths:
# - relative filenames (with and without directories)
# - absolute Unix-like paths
# - Windows-like paths (drive letters, backslashes)
# - dot/parent components (., ..)
# - different file extensions (bmp recommended for debug image)
# - directories for texture search paths
# - mixed UTF-8 characters (where valid) to exercise encoding handling
# All strings are NUL-terminated. The overall buffer <= 4096 bytes.

SAFE_UTF8 = [
    "αβ", "✓", "漢字", "🚀", "ñ", "é"
]

BMP_BASENAMES = [
    "debug.bmp", "frame.bmp", "out.bmp", "capture.bmp", "dump.bmp", "pm.bmp"
]

EXTS = [".bmp", ".png", ".jpg", ""]

REL_DIRS = [
    ".", "..", "textures", "assets", "data", "images", "gfx", "skins", "presets"
]

ABS_UNIX_DIRS = [
    "/tmp", "/var/tmp", "/var/run", "/usr/local/share", "/home/user", "/mnt/ramdisk"
]

ABS_WIN_DIRS = [
    "C:/Temp", "C:/Users/Public", "C:/Windows/Temp", "D:/data", "E:/assets"
]

# Helper builders

def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, seq: List[str]) -> str:
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]


def _rand_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Prefer bmp for the debug image suggestion but allow others
    base = _rand_choice(rng, BMP_BASENAMES)
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        # randomize basename
        stem = "img" + str(rng.randrange(10000)).zfill(4)
        ext = _rand_choice(rng, EXTS)
        base = stem + ext if ext else stem + ".bmp"
    parts = []
    # choose path style
    style = rng.choice(["rel", "unix", "win"])  # keep valid but diverse
    if style == "rel":
        # relative path possibly in a subdir
        depth = rng.randrange(0, 3)
        parts.extend(rng.choices(REL_DIRS, k=depth))
        # optionally include UTF-8 directory
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            parts.append("textures-" + _rand_choice(rng, SAFE_UTF8))
        parts.append(base)
        path = "/".join([p for p in parts if p and p != "."]) if parts else base
    elif style == "unix":
        root = _rand_choice(rng, ABS_UNIX_DIRS)
        depth = rng.randrange(0, 3)
        mid = []
        for _ in range(depth):
            name = rng.choice([
                "set", "tex", "images", "subdir", "..", "."
            ])
            if name not in (".",):
                mid.append(name)
        # optionally utf8 folder
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            mid.append("u-" + _rand_choice(rng, SAFE_UTF8))
        path = root.rstrip("/") + "/" + "/".join(mid + [base]) if mid else root.rstrip("/") + "/" + base
    else:  # win
        root = _rand_choice(rng, ABS_WIN_DIRS)
        depth = rng.randrange(0, 3)
        mid = []
        for _ in range(depth):
            name = rng.choice(["set", "tex", "images", "subdir", "..", "."])
            if name not in (".",):
                mid.append(name)
        # Windows uses backslashes commonly; accept mixed but valid
        sep = "\\"
        path = root.replace("/", sep)
        if mid:
            path += sep + sep.join(mid)
        path += sep + base
    return path


def _rand_directory(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build directories used by texture search paths
    style = rng.choice(["rel", "unix", "win"])
    if style == "rel":
        parts = []
        depth = rng.randrange(0, 3)
        parts.extend(rng.choices(REL_DIRS, k=depth))
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            parts.append("dir-" + _rand_choice(rng, SAFE_UTF8))
        path = "/".join([p for p in parts if p]) or _rand_choice(rng, REL_DIRS)
    elif style == "unix":
        root = _rand_choice(rng, ABS_UNIX_DIRS)
        depth = rng.randrange(0, 3)
        mid = rng.choices(["textures", "assets", "images", "presets", "skins"], k=depth)
        path = root.rstrip("/")
        if mid:
            path += "/" + "/".join(mid)
    else:
        root = _rand_choice(rng, ABS_WIN_DIRS)
        depth = rng.randrange(0, 3)
        mid = rng.choices(["textures", "assets", "images", "presets", "skins"], k=depth)
        path = root.replace("/", "\\")
        if mid:
            path += "\\" + "\\".join(mid)
    return path


def _emit_cstr_list(strings: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Join as NUL-terminated strings, with a final extra NUL to give space for empty reads
    out = bytearray()
    for s in strings:
        # ensure no embedded NULs; they would truncate in C-strings
        s2 = s.replace("\x00", "")
        out.extend(s2.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore"))
        out.append(0)
    # Provide an empty string too to allow the fuzzer to pick it if it asks more than we provide
    out.append(0)
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide how many directory paths to include for projectm_set_texture_search_paths
    dir_count = rng.randrange(0, 9)  # 0..8 as per stub max_entries
    dirs = []
    for _ in range(dir_count):
        d = _rand_directory(rng)
        # Sometimes include trailing separator
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            if "\\" in d and "/" not in d:
                d = d + "\\"
            else:
                d = d.rstrip("/") + "/"
        dirs.append(d)

    # One filename for projectm_write_debug_image_on_next_frame
    filename = _rand_filename(rng)

    # Additionally include a few alternates to seed the FUZZ_PARAM pool
    alternates = [
        "debug-" + str(rng.randrange(100000)) + ".bmp",
        "./out.bmp",
        "../capture.bmp",
        "/tmp/projectm-" + str(rng.randrange(10000)) + ".bmp",
        "C:/Temp/pm-" + str(rng.randrange(10000)) + ".bmp",
    ]

    # Aggregate all strings. Place filename early so the first FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME can pick it.
    strings = [filename] + dirs + alternates

    # Ensure total size <= 4096
    buf = _emit_cstr_list(strings)
    if len(buf) > 4096:
        # Trim by reducing alternates/dirs
        keep = []
        for s in strings:
            keep.append(s)
            if len(_emit_cstr_list(keep)) > 4096:
                keep.pop()
                break
        buf = _emit_cstr_list(keep)

    return buf

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Target data type: arbitrary binary string carried in std::string. It may contain any bytes including NULs.
# Fuzzer stub usage:
# - projectm_set_log_callback uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR once to create a std::string user_data buffer and passes its data() as void*.
#   The library does not interpret the contents; it only stores/returns the pointer. Therefore, any bytes are valid.
#   Interesting cases: empty buffer, very small/large buffers, buffers with embedded NULs, high-bit bytes, repeated patterns,
#   UTF-8-like text, and aligned sizes. We must keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL_SIZE = 4096

def _rand_bytes(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _pattern_repeat(pattern: bytes, length: int) -> bytes:
    if not pattern:
        return b""
    return (pattern * (length // len(pattern) + 1))[:length]

def _utf8_like(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Produce mostly-valid UTF-8 with occasional invalid sequences and NULs
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < n:
        choice = r.random()
        if choice < 0.55:
            # ASCII
            out.append(r.randrange(0x20, 0x7F))
        elif choice < 0.60:
            out.append(0)  # NUL
        elif choice < 0.78:
            # 2-byte sequence
            c1 = r.randrange(0xC2, 0xDF + 1)
            c2 = r.randrange(0x80, 0xBF + 1)
            out += bytes([c1, c2])
        elif choice < 0.92:
            # 3-byte sequence
            c1 = r.randrange(0xE0, 0xEF + 1)
            c2 = r.randrange(0x80, 0xBF + 1)
            c3 = r.randrange(0x80, 0xBF + 1)
            out += bytes([c1, c2, c3])
        elif choice < 0.97:
            # 4-byte sequence
            c1 = r.randrange(0xF0, 0xF4 + 1)
            out += bytes([c1, r.randrange(0x80, 0xBF + 1), r.randrange(0x80, 0xBF + 1), r.randrange(0x80, 0xBF + 1)])
        else:
            # Intentionally invalid leading byte
            out.append(r.randrange(0x80, 0xC1))
    return bytes(out[:n])

def _aligned_block(r: random.Random, n: int, align: int) -> bytes:
    # Create a block with a header indicating size, then pad to alignment with a pattern
    header = struct.pack('<I', n)
    rem = max(0, n - len(header))
    body = _rand_bytes(r, rem)
    block = header + body
    pad_len = (align - (len(block) % align)) % align
    pad = _pattern_repeat(b"\xAA\x55", pad_len)
    return (block + pad)[:n]

def _cases(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    # Curated set of interesting buffers
    sizes = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256, 511, 512, 1024, 2048]
    # Ensure we don't exceed MAX_TOTAL_SIZE for each buffer
    sizes = [s for s in sizes if s <= MAX_TOTAL_SIZE]

    fixed_patterns = [
        b"",  # empty
        b"\x00",  # single NUL
        b"\xFF",
        b"A",
        b"user_data",
        b"projectM-log-cb",
        bytes(range(256)),  # 0..255
        b"\x00\xFF" * 32,
    ]

    results: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Fixed patterns expanded to various sizes
    for pat in fixed_patterns:
        for s in r.sample(sizes, k=min(len(sizes), 5)):
            results.append(_pattern_repeat(pat, s))

    # 2) UTF-8-like content
    for s in r.sample(sizes, k=min(len(sizes), 6)):
        results.append(_utf8_like(r, s))

    # 3) Random bytes of selected sizes
    for s in r.sample(sizes, k=min(len(sizes), 6)):
        results.append(_rand_bytes(r, s))

    # 4) Aligned header-like blocks
    for s in r.sample(sizes, k=min(len(sizes), 6)):
        align = r.choice([4, 8, 16, 32, 64])
        results.append(_aligned_block(r, s, align))

    # 5) Boundary-heavy content around pointer-aligned sizes
    for base in [0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 15, 31, 63]:
        s = min(MAX_TOTAL_SIZE, base)
        results.append(_pattern_repeat(b"\xDE\xAD\xBE\xEF", s))

    # 6) Include one max-sized buffer close to limit with mixed content
    big_size = min(3072 + r.randrange(0, 1024), MAX_TOTAL_SIZE)
    chunk_a = _pattern_repeat(b"\x00\xFF", big_size // 4)
    chunk_b = _utf8_like(r, big_size // 4)
    chunk_c = _rand_bytes(r, big_size - len(chunk_a) - len(chunk_b))
    results.append(chunk_a + chunk_b + chunk_c)

    return results

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    candidates = _cases(r)
    # Select one candidate deterministically from the seeded RNG, but also vary selection
    idx = r.randrange(len(candidates))
    return candidates[idx]

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator targets identifier strings used by projectm_sprite_create:
# - type: prefers known keyword "milkdrop" (case-insensitive), but we also
#   produce other plausible identifiers to explore failure paths.
# - code: for type "milkdrop", expects contents similar to an imgNN section.
#   We'll emit small, valid-looking Milkdrop sprite code snippets.
# The fuzzer will request buffers via FUZZ_PARAM_STR for both fields; we return
# a single bytes blob that contains two null-terminated C strings back-to-back:
#   [type\0][code\0]
# so the harness can split or reuse appropriately. If it does not split, using
# the first NUL-terminated token as type and the remainder as code is still
# workable because both tokens are valid C strings.

_MAX_TOTAL = 4096

_KNOWN_TYPES = [
    "milkdrop",
    # Some alternates to exercise case-insensitive paths
    "MILKDROP",
    "MilkDrop",
]

# Minimal, valid-looking Milkdrop sprite code (imgNN content style). We vary a few
# numeric parameters and flags. Milkdrop img sections typically look like:
#   zoom 1.0
#   rot 0.0
#   x 0.5
#   y 0.5
#   image_sampler <int>
#   image_url <string>
# The engine here expects the contents of an imgNN section; we'll keep to simple
# key/value lines commonly seen.
_BASE_IMG_TEMPLATES: List[str] = [
    "zoom {zoom}\nrot {rot}\nx {x}\ny {y}\nimage_sampler {sampler}\nimage_url {url}\n",
    "x {x}\ny {y}\nzoom {zoom}\nalpha {alpha}\nblend {blend}\nimage_url {url}\n",
    "zoom {zoom}\nrot {rot}\nwarp {warp}\nimage_sampler {sampler}\nimage_url {url}\n",
]

_IMG_URLS = [
    "tex://noise",
    "tex://logo",
    "file://textures/flake.png",
    "file://textures/dot.bmp",
    "idle://",
]

_DEF_OTHER_TYPES = [
    # Unsupported types to cover failure paths
    "svg", "png", "bitmap", "shader", "sprite", "milk", "drop",
]


def _rand_float(rng: random.Random, a: float, b: float) -> float:
    return rng.uniform(a, b)


def _pick_type(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Bias towards milkdrop 70% of the time to hit success paths more often
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        return rng.choice(_KNOWN_TYPES)
    # Otherwise return a plausible but likely-unsupported identifier
    # Mix in random casing and dashes/underscores sometimes
    base = rng.choice(_DEF_OTHER_TYPES + [
        "custom", "experimental", "sprite2d", "spr", "mdrop", "milkdrop2"
    ])
    # Apply random case
    mode = rng.randint(0, 3)
    if mode == 1:
        base = base.upper()
    elif mode == 2:
        base = base.capitalize()
    # Maybe add a suffix/prefix
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        base = base + str(rng.randint(0, 9))
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        base = "type_" + base
    return base


def _gen_milkdrop_code(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    tmpl = rng.choice(_BASE_IMG_TEMPLATES)
    code = tmpl.format(
        zoom=round(_rand_float(rng, 0.1, 3.0), 3),
        rot=round(_rand_float(rng, -3.141, 3.141), 3),
        x=round(_rand_float(rng, 0.0, 1.0), 3),
        y=round(_rand_float(rng, 0.0, 1.0), 3),
        sampler=rng.randint(0, 3),
        url=rng.choice(_IMG_URLS),
        alpha=round(_rand_float(rng, 0.0, 1.0), 3),
        blend=rng.randint(0, 1),
        warp=round(_rand_float(rng, 0.0, 1.0), 3),
    )
    # Optionally add some extra well-formed lines
    extras = []
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        extras.append(f"grid_w {rng.randint(8, 64)}")
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        extras.append(f"grid_h {rng.randint(8, 64)}")
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        extras.append(f"tex_wrap {rng.randint(0, 1)}")
    if extras:
        code += "\n".join(extras) + "\n"
    # Keep size modest
    return code


def _gen_other_code(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Produce a harmless generic key=value style block; still a valid C string.
    keys = ["name", "version", "author", "flags", "note"]
    lines = []
    for k in keys:
        if rng.random() < 0.8:
            if k == "version":
                val = f"{rng.randint(0, 3)}.{rng.randint(0, 9)}"
            elif k == "flags":
                val = ",".join(rng.sample(["alpha", "blend", "wrap", "repeat", "nearest"],
                                           rng.randint(1, 3)))
            elif k == "note":
                val = rng.choice(["test", "demo", "fallback", "unknown"])
            else:
                val = rng.choice(["sprite", "example", "custom"]) + str(rng.randint(0, 99))
            lines.append(f"{k}={val}")
    # Add a couple of numeric params
    lines.append(f"width={rng.randint(8,512)}")
    lines.append(f"height={rng.randint(8,512)}")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def _build_payload(type_str: str, code_str: str) -> bytes:
    # Join as two NUL-terminated strings, within size limit
    t = type_str.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore") + b"\x00"
    c = code_str.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore") + b"\x00"
    payload = t + c
    if len(payload) > _MAX_TOTAL:
        # Truncate code to fit
        max_c = max(0, _MAX_TOTAL - len(t) - 1)
        c = code_str.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")[:max_c] + b"\x00"
        payload = t + c
    return payload


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    t = _pick_type(rng)
    if t.lower() == "milkdrop":
        c = _gen_milkdrop_code(rng)
    else:
        c = _gen_other_code(rng)
    return _build_payload(t, c)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for Milkdrop sprite (imgNN section) code strings.
# We aim to create valid-looking Milkdrop sprite definitions that projectM can parse
# when type == "milkdrop". The fuzzer stub feeds our bytes to FUZZ_PARAM_STR for both
# type and code. We therefore emit a textual blob that includes multiple candidate
# sections: a primary well-formed img section plus some extras, so different substrings
# can still be useful. The blob is null-terminated by the harness when converted to C strings.

# Milkdrop img section quick structure (commonly accepted by projectM):
# [imgN]
# enabled=1
# code: <per-frame/per-vertex equations optional>
# x=.., y=.., w=.., h=..
# tex_wrap=0/1, additive=0/1, rot=.., zoom=..
# more flags: alpha, r, g, b, border_r/g/b/a, blendmode, src/channel, etc.
# texture controls: rand_start, tile, stretch, tint, etc. Implemented options vary.

# We generate a mix of:
# - Minimal valid sections
# - Rich sections with many fields
# - Edge-case numeric ranges and booleans
# - Multiple img indices to explore parser state

SAFE_NAMES = [
    "enabled", "x", "y", "w", "h", "zoom", "rot", "alpha",
    "r", "g", "b", "additive", "tex_wrap", "tile", "stretch",
    "blendmode", "rand_start", "src", "channel", "border_r", "border_g", "border_b", "border_a",
    "anchor", "tint", "draw", "scale_x", "scale_y", "offset_x", "offset_y",
]

BOOLS = [0, 1]
BLENDMODES = [0, 1, 2]
CHANNELS = [0, 1]


def rnd_float(rng: random.Random, a: float, b: float) -> float:
    return rng.uniform(a, b)


def rnd_int(rng: random.Random, a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return rng.randint(a, b)


def fmt_f(x: float) -> str:
    # Milkdrop often uses decimal points; keep a few decimals
    return f"{x:.6f}".rstrip("0").rstrip(".")


def header_for_index(idx: int) -> str:
    return f"[img{idx}]\n"


def minimal_section(rng: random.Random, idx: int) -> str:
    # A small, likely-accepted section
    x = fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, -2.0, 2.0))
    y = fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, -2.0, 2.0))
    w = fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, 0.01, 2.0))
    h = fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, 0.01, 2.0))
    enabled = rng.choice(BOOLS)
    additive = rng.choice(BOOLS)
    tex_wrap = rng.choice(BOOLS)
    alpha = fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, 0.0, 1.0))
    rot = fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, -360.0, 360.0))

    lines = [
        header_for_index(idx),
        f"enabled={enabled}\n",
        f"x={x}\n",
        f"y={y}\n",
        f"w={w}\n",
        f"h={h}\n",
        f"alpha={alpha}\n",
        f"additive={additive}\n",
        f"tex_wrap={tex_wrap}\n",
        f"rot={rot}\n",
        "\n",
    ]
    return "".join(lines)


def rich_section(rng: random.Random, idx: int) -> str:
    x = fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, -5.0, 5.0))
    y = fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, -5.0, 5.0))
    w = fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, 0.01, 5.0))
    h = fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, 0.01, 5.0))

    fields = {
        "enabled": str(rng.choice(BOOLS)),
        "x": x,
        "y": y,
        "w": w,
        "h": h,
        "zoom": fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, 0.1, 4.0)),
        "rot": fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, -720.0, 720.0)),
        "alpha": fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, 0.0, 1.0)),
        "r": fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, 0.0, 1.0)),
        "g": fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, 0.0, 1.0)),
        "b": fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, 0.0, 1.0)),
        "additive": str(rng.choice(BOOLS)),
        "tex_wrap": str(rng.choice(BOOLS)),
        "tile": str(rng.choice(BOOLS)),
        "stretch": str(rng.choice(BOOLS)),
        "blendmode": str(rng.choice(BLENDMODES)),
        "rand_start": str(rng.choice(BOOLS)),
        "src": str(rng.choice([0, 1, 2])),
        "channel": str(rng.choice(CHANNELS)),
        "border_r": fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, 0.0, 1.0)),
        "border_g": fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, 0.0, 1.0)),
        "border_b": fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, 0.0, 1.0)),
        "border_a": fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, 0.0, 1.0)),
        "anchor": str(rng.choice([0, 1, 2, 3])),
        "tint": fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, 0.0, 2.0)),
        "draw": str(rng.choice(BOOLS)),
        "scale_x": fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, 0.1, 3.0)),
        "scale_y": fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, 0.1, 3.0)),
        "offset_x": fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, -2.0, 2.0)),
        "offset_y": fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, -2.0, 2.0)),
    }

    lines = [header_for_index(idx)]

    # Optional code block: simple per-frame style expressions
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        lines.append("code:\n")
        # Include a few lines referencing time/beat-like variables often present
        code_lines = []
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            code_lines.append(f"    rot = rot + {fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, -0.05, 0.05))};\n")
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            code_lines.append(f"    alpha = {fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, 0.2, 1.0))};\n")
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            code_lines.append(f"    x = x + sin(time*{fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, 0.5, 4.0))})*{fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, 0.0, 0.2))};\n")
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            code_lines.append(f"    y = y + cos(time*{fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, 0.5, 4.0))})*{fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, 0.0, 0.2))};\n")
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            code_lines.append(f"    r = {fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, 0.0, 1.0))}; g = {fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, 0.0, 1.0))}; b = {fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, 0.0, 1.0))};\n")
        lines.extend(code_lines)

    # Emit fields in varied order
    keys = list(fields.keys())
    rng.shuffle(keys)
    for k in keys:
        lines.append(f"{k}={fields[k]}\n")

    lines.append("\n")
    return "".join(lines)


def variant_noise(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Add extra unrelated key-value or comments to explore parser leniency, but keep valid overall
    pieces: List[str] = []
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        pieces.append("; comment: generated by seed-based generator\n")
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
        k = rng.choice(SAFE_NAMES)
        v = rng.choice([
            fmt_f(rnd_float(rng, -3.0, 3.0)),
            str(rng.choice(BOOLS)),
            str(rng.choice(BLENDMODES)),
        ])
        pieces.append(f"{k}={v}\n")
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        pieces.append("\n")
    return "".join(pieces)


def build_blob(rng: random.Random, target_size: int) -> str:
    # Compose multiple sections to exercise parser across indices
    sections: List[str] = []

    count = rng.randint(1, 4)
    used_indices = set()
    for _ in range(count):
        # Unique but plausible indices in Milkdrop style (0..9 common, but allow larger)
        idx = rng.randint(0, 9)
        # Ensure uniqueness to avoid unintended overwrites
        while idx in used_indices:
            idx = rng.randint(0, 9)
        used_indices.add(idx)

        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            sections.append(minimal_section(rng, idx))
        else:
            sections.append(rich_section(rng, idx))

        # Insert some benign noise between sections
        sections.append(variant_noise(rng))

    blob = "".join(sections)

    # Keep within size limit; trim if needed while staying syntactically okay
    if len(blob) > target_size:
        blob = blob[:target_size]
        # Ensure final line ends with newline
        if not blob.endswith("\n"):
            last_nl = blob.rfind("\n")
            if last_nl != -1:
                blob = blob[: last_nl + 1]
            else:
                blob = "[img0]\nenabled=1\n\n"

    return blob


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Aim for a mid-sized, rich blob but cap total size to 4096
    # Provide some variability with seed while keeping well-formed
    target_size = rng.randint(256, 1400)

    blob = build_blob(rng, target_size)

    # Return as bytes; fuzzer stub will use this for FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    return blob.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
